original.target_description: Single main experiment (supplied study 1): male undergraduates rated preferences for music and memory activities before anticipated confrontational versus nonconfrontational games. Target is the within-subjects Game Type × Emotion interaction in the Game Type × Emotion × Activity Type repeated-measures ANOVA, Emotional Preferences results and Figure 1.

n.sample_role: Male undergraduate participants in the repeated-measures emotional-preference analysis; total main sample corroborated by target ANOVA denominator df 162 for the three-level within-subject emotion factor.
n.exclusions: Only males were recruited/included (p. 325 footnote 1). No further exclusions or missing preference observations reported; the target degrees of freedom are consistent with the stated 82 participants.
n.location: Published p. 325 (PDF p. 2), Method—Participants; p. 326 (PDF p. 3), Results—Emotional Preferences.

es.location: Published p. 326 (PDF p. 3), Results—Emotional Preferences, Game Type × Emotion interaction (Figure 1).

p.location: Published p. 326 (PDF p. 3), Results—Emotional Preferences, same Game Type × Emotion interaction.

notes:
Replication values are author-derived primary master-table values, retained as printed. Corrupted Greek metric labels preserved; no conversion performed. Table sample N is not independently established as analytic N. Original: DOI landing returned 403; OpenAlex/Unpaywall supplied no open-access full-text location; additional available author/repository routes did not yield the full original. Replication-source original statistics were not substituted. 
Source follow-up: Fresh original-only validation. Supplied published article title/authors match the reference; rendered PDF pp. 2–3 (published pp. 325–326) visually checked. The supplied canonical text encodes printed equals signs as "5" and multiplication signs as U+0002; exact quotations preserve canonical glyphs. On the rendered target page the test reads F(2, 162) = 192.89, p < .001; the value 192.89 is the requested printed test statistic, not an effect-size conversion. The main sample of eighty-two is visually confirmed; its use for the target analysis is supported by the repeated-measures design and target degrees of freedom, rather than a separately printed analytic-N label. No manuscript/appendix substitution. Replication and narrative replication success are outside the assigned target.
